tasks.title: The MG team never reloads; Clip.ReloadStoop cannot be reached
tasks.why: AnimationController.cs:697 guards the reload rung with `arche != 2`, so the machinegunner never enters it. Two things follow. First, the clip picked inside is `low ? (inTrench || arche != 2 ? Clip.ReloadKneel : Clip.ReloadStoop) : Clip.ReloadStand` (line 700): `ReloadStoop` needs `arche == 2`, which the guard above has already excluded, so that arm of the ternary is dead and the `inTrench ||` in front of it is noise. ReloadStoop is a real baked row (Editor/InfantryClipTable.cs:55, "Reload" over "Crouch Idle", 2.4 s in the table) that nothing in the game can play. Second, and the part the player sees: the MG's magazine is 50 (line 660) and `s.Shots` is only ever zeroed inside that block (line 699), so an MG team fires belt after belt for the whole match with no reload beat, the one infantry archetype of the four with no reload animation at all, while `s.Shots` (ushort) climbs until it wraps at 65,535. Read in code, not confirmed in Play.
tasks.done_when: an EditMode test on InfantryFiringTests' rig ticks a standing machinegunner (archetype 2) past 50 Shot events with a long FireCooldown and asserts he plays a reload clip and that State[man].Shots fell back to 0; and either ReloadStoop is reached by the crouched MG or it is dropped from the table and the bake row with it

tasks.title: A kneeling man never plays a turn clip: five baked turns are dead
tasks.why: The turn rung is gated `if (math.abs(turn) > 1.05f && target >= 0 && !low)` (AnimationController.cs:765) and picks only Turn90L/Turn90R/Turn180 (line 767). `low` is `s.Stance == Crouch` (line 512), so no crouched or stooping man ever starts a turn clip, and Clip.KneelTurn90L, KneelTurn90R, StoopTurn90L, StoopTurn90R and StoopTurn180 are never asked for anywhere in the project (grep: only the table at lines 94-98) even though all five are baked from their own Mixamo files (Editor/InfantryClipTable.cs:74-75) and lines 97-98 carry a measured `Turn` for each, which only Start and Advance read for clips that actually play. What the player gets instead: line 771 sets `s.BodyYaw = faceTo` and Advance eases the drawn yaw at 3 rad/s for a non-locomotion rung (line 918), so a kneeling garrison man who picks up a target behind him swivels a full half-turn on the spot in about a second with his feet sliding through the kneeling idle. The trench garrison spends most of a match in exactly that stance (the trench routine's base is KneelIdle), so this is the common case, not the corner. Read in code, not confirmed in Play.
tasks.done_when: an EditMode test places a kneeling man (StanceOf = Crouch) with a target 150 degrees behind him, ticks the controller, and asserts State[man].Rung == Rung.Turn with a KneelTurn/StoopTurn clip; the drawn yaw must not move more than the clip's own Turn while it plays

tasks.title: The debrief counts every destroyed vehicle as a man lost
tasks.why: SimWorld.Despawn emits a Death event for EVERY slot (SimWorld.cs:259, unconditional) and then a VehicleDestroyed on top of it when the slot was a vehicle (line 262). MatchStats takes the two as separate things: MatchStats.cs:63 `case SimEventType.Death: menLost[TeamOf(ev.A)]++;` with no vehicle test at all, and line 64 counts the same slot again under vehiclesLost. So the debrief's MEN LOST (DebriefScreen.cs:37 fills men-lost from report.MenLost) is inflated by exactly the number of tanks, armoured cars and walkers that side lost, and the same slot is reported twice on one plate: a side that lost 40 men and 6 machines reads 46 / 6. MenFielded has the mirror of it: line 65 counts UnitSpawned for every slot, so a deployed tank is a man fielded as well. A subscriber cannot even recover the truth from the flags, because Despawn zeroes Flags[slot] (line 256) before the event is dispatched - the vehicle bit is gone by then, which is presumably how this got past the author. Nothing guards it: tasks.md:306 says 'Nothing tests MatchStats or ObjectiveTracker directly'. Read in code, not confirmed in Play.
tasks.done_when: a new EditMode test builds a world, spawns one man and one tank per side, despawns both, and asserts the report reads MenLost 1 and VehiclesLost 1 for that team (not 2 and 1), and the same for MenFielded; it must go red on today's MatchStats

tasks.title: DeathGagTests guards the gag maths with the gag maths' own constants
tasks.why: Three of the loudest numbers in DeathGags are asserted against themselves. DeathGagTests.cs:250-251 says `Assert.AreEqual(DeathGags.RocketFar, after.x / before.x)` and `AreEqual(math.min(DeathGags.RocketHigh * before.y, HighCap), after.y)`, which is DeathGags.cs:172 (`far *= Towards(1f, RocketFar, a)`, a = 1) written out a second time: retune RocketFar or RocketHigh and the test still passes, and so it would if the factor were applied to the wrong intensity curve. Line 103 is `Assert.AreEqual(1f, DeathGags.DefaultIntensity)`, a restatement of the constant one line of the production file above. Line 173, `Assert.AreEqual(-32, rec.Gag.RestQ, "an eighth of his height")`, sits exactly on VatTintCode's clamp floor (DeathGags.cs:258 clamps to -32; a pancake at 0.12 maps to -32.0), so any squash at or below 0.12, including 0 or a negative height, reads the same -32 and passes. Cost: the rocket's reach and the pancake's flatness look guarded and are not, which is how the camera look's clamp-restating asserts got found twice over.
tasks.done_when: the three asserts quote a measured number instead of the production constant (e.g. the rocket's throw in metres against the plain throw, and a RestQ bound strictly inside the clamp, say <= -24 and > -32), and flipping RocketFar, RocketHigh or the pancake's 0.12 in DeathGags.cs makes DeathGagTests go red

tasks.title: A bench's fx.quality knob never reaches the effects' tier
tasks.why: Two [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(BeforeSceneLoad)] hooks race, and the effects' tier loses. SettingsApplier.cs:44-45 (ApplyAudioOnLaunch) is the ONLY production caller of ApplyEffects, and ApplyEffects reads the knob once, there: FxQuality.Apply -> Knobs.Get("fx.quality", -1). PerfBench.cs:85-99 is the other BeforeSceneLoad hook, and the bench string's knobs only enter Knobs at its line 99 (Knobs.Parse(o.Knobs)). Unity does not order RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethods across classes, and nothing re-applies the tier afterwards - grep across the project finds FxQuality.Apply at exactly one site and FxQuality.Set only in tests. So `knobs=fx.quality=0` in a bench string pins nothing except by load-order luck: the run draws at whatever tier settings.json resolved to (High by default) while the report says LOW, and every number it measured is a High number filed under the wrong tier. The knob is advertised as a bench's handle in FxQuality.cs:6 and in StaticLifecycleTests.cs:30 ('a bench pins it with the knob fx.quality'), and FxQualityTests only ever exercises the pure Resolve(setting, level, count, knob) - 'the knob wins over both' is asserted on the function, never on the wiring, which is why a knob that reaches nothing reads green. Read in code, not confirmed in a bench run.
tasks.done_when: a test sets the knob fx.quality after launch (Knobs.Set) and asserts FxQuality.Tier follows it, and a bench run with knobs=fx.quality=0 reports Low in its summary with a Low chunk cap in force; the test goes red on today's code
